steps.title: Import Vue and ref from Vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the Vue package to enable reactive state.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing functions from a module
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary Vue APIs imported for creating reactive state in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref, which are essential for reactive state management in Vue components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect or incomplete. Remember to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named ControlledVsUncontrolled with a template and script section. The template should contain a single root <div> element.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component typically has a <template> section for markup and a <script> section for JavaScript logic.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: basic Vue component structure
steps.seedCode:
<template>
  <!-- Add a single root <div> element here -->
</template>

<script>
export default {
  name: 'ControlledVsUncontrolled'
}
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component with the correct name and basic structure is created.
successCriteria: The component is named ControlledVsUncontrolled, has a template with a single root <div>, and exports the component object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component structure. This gives us a foundation to build our controlled and uncontrolled input examples.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both template and script sections, the component is named 'ControlledVsUncontrolled', and the template has a single root <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a Vue component with a template containing a single root <div> and a script section that exports a component object named 'ControlledVsUncontrolled'.

steps.title: Initialize controlled input state
steps.instruction: Inside the component's script options, use ref to create a reactive state variable named 'controlledValue' and initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Add a data property that returns an object containing the ref declaration.
steps.seedCode:
<template>
  <!-- Add a single root <div> element here -->
</template>

<script>
export default {
  name: 'ControlledVsUncontrolled',
  data() {
    return {
      // Create controlledValue ref here
    }
  }
}
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have reactive state ready to bind to a controlled input field.
successCriteria: The component's data function returns an object with a 'controlledValue' property initialized as ref('').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state for the controlled input using Vue's ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() to create the reactive state and initializing it with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a reactive state variable named 'controlledValue' using ref() inside the data function.

steps.title: Define handler for controlled input
steps.instruction: Inside the component's methods object, define a method named 'updateControlledValue' that takes an event parameter and updates the 'controlledValue' data property with the input's current value.
steps.hint: Add a methods property to the component configuration and define a function that sets this.controlledValue to event.target.value.
steps.seedCode:
<template>
  <!-- Add a single root <div> element here -->
</template>

<script>
export default {
  name: 'ControlledVsUncontrolled',
  data() {
    return {
      controlledValue: ''
    }
  },
  // Define updateControlledValue method here
}
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a method that will handle input change events and update the controlled state.
successCriteria: A method named 'updateControlledValue' is defined in the methods object, takes an event parameter, and sets this.controlledValue to event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the event handler that will update the controlled state when the input changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a method, but check that it's in the methods object, takes an event parameter, and properly updates controlledValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't defined correctly. Make sure to add a methods property with an updateControlledValue function that updates the controlledValue data property.

steps.title: Add controlled input field to template
steps.instruction: Inside the template's root <div>, add an <input> element with v-model bound to controlledValue.
steps.hint: Use v-model to create a two-way binding between the input and the controlledValue data property.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: binding an input to a data property -->
<input v-model="userInput">
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an input field that is controlled by the component's data.
successCriteria: An <input> element with v-model="controlledValue" is present in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a controlled input field. The v-model binding ensures the input's value is synchronized with the component's data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an <input> element with v-model="controlledValue" inside the template's root <div>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The controlled input field is missing. Add an <input> element with v-model="controlledValue" to the template.

steps.title: Display controlled input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the template to display the current value of controlledValue.
steps.hint:
Use a

tag and display the controlledValue data property using Vue's template syntax.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a data property in Vue template

{{ message }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show a paragraph that displays the current value of the controlled input field.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added to the template that displays the controlledValue data property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph to display the current controlled input value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a paragraph element that displays the controlledValue property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element displaying controlledValue is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add uncontrolled input field
steps.instruction: Add a second input element to your template with a ref attribute named 'uncontrolledInput' to create an uncontrolled input.
steps.hint: Use the ref attribute on an input element to create a reference to it. This allows you to access its value directly without binding it to data.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: creating a ref for an input -->
<input type="text" ref="myInput" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain two input elements: one controlled (with v-model) and one uncontrolled (with ref).
successCriteria: An input element with ref="uncontrolledInput" is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an uncontrolled input field using a ref attribute.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an input element with the ref attribute set to 'uncontrolledInput'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The uncontrolled input field is missing or incorrect. Add an input element with ref="uncontrolledInput" to the template.

steps.title: Create ref for uncontrolled input
steps.instruction: In the script section, create a ref named 'uncontrolledInput' to reference the uncontrolled input element you'll add later.
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create a reactive reference that can hold a DOM element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a ref for an input element
const inputRef = ref(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The script section will include a ref declaration for the uncontrolled input element.
successCriteria: A ref named 'uncontrolledInput' is created in the component's script section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref to reference the uncontrolled input element. This ref will allow you to access the DOM element directly without using v-model.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a ref named 'uncontrolledInput' in the script section. Remember to use the ref function from Vue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref for the uncontrolled input hasn't been created yet. You need to add a ref declaration in the script section to reference the DOM element directly.

steps.title: Define handler to read uncontrolled value
steps.instruction: Inside the component's methods object, define a method called 'getUncontrolledValue' that reads the current value from the uncontrolled input ref.
steps.hint: Create a method that accesses the ref's value property. In Vue, you can access refs via this.$refs.
steps.expectedOutcome: A method named getUncontrolledValue is defined in the methods object that reads from this.$refs.
successCriteria: The component has a getUncontrolledValue method that accesses this.$refs to read the uncontrolled input's value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a method to read the uncontrolled input's value via refs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a method called getUncontrolledValue that accesses this.$refs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't defined correctly. Check that it's in the methods object and accesses this.$refs.

steps.title: Add button to read uncontrolled value
steps.instruction: Add a button element to your template that calls the handler to read the uncontrolled input value when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the v-on directive (or @ shorthand) to attach a click event handler to the button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Read Value</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that, when clicked, will trigger the handler to read the uncontrolled input value.
successCriteria: The template includes a button element with a click event handler that calls the appropriate method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a button that will read the uncontrolled input value when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has a click event handler that calls the method to read the uncontrolled value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct click handler. Add a button with @click or v-on:click to call the handler.

steps.title: Display uncontrolled input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element in your template to display the value read from the uncontrolled input. Use the same variable name you'll use to store the uncontrolled value.
steps.hint:
Add a

tag in your template section, similar to how you displayed the controlled value. You'll need to reference the variable that holds the uncontrolled input's value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value in Vue template

{{ uncontrolledValue }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element will be added to the template, ready to display the uncontrolled input value once you implement the logic to read it.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template with appropriate Vue template syntax to display a value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the paragraph element that will display the uncontrolled input value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it uses the correct Vue template syntax for displaying values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element for displaying the uncontrolled value is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add comparison explanation
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph in the template that explains the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs.
steps.hint:
Add a

tag with text that summarizes the key difference: controlled inputs use v-model and reactive data, while uncontrolled inputs use refs and manual value access.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding explanatory text

Controlled inputs update state automatically, uncontrolled inputs need manual reading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template includes a paragraph that clearly explains the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with explanatory text about controlled vs uncontrolled inputs is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a clear explanation comparing controlled and uncontrolled inputs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it explains the difference between controlled (v-model) and uncontrolled (refs) approaches.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph explaining the difference between controlled and uncontrolled inputs is missing or incorrect.
